label: vanilla-1836-wages-n5
_why: THE 1836 VANILLA REFERENCE, PROPERLY: n=5 for variance, and WAGES included so the rebase can replace config/measured_1836.json in full rather than in part. The n=3 attempt established that the start is stable (production -0%, sell -1%, workforce -1%, urban centres -1%) but carried NO wages block, and measured_1836.json is documented as silently wrong rather than obviously missing when stale — so a partial overwrite would have deleted the measured base weekly wage the whole scenario wage model runs on.
_arms: {kind: control} — vanilla + telemetry and nothing else. This measures THE GAME, so it must not carry our content; a modded arm here would rebase the scenarios on ourselves.
_comparison: Against config/measured_1836.json as it stands (extracted 2026-08-03) and against what extract_presets.ps1 derives from the history files. Differences get reported, not silently applied — the history files are the AUTHORED start and the save is the INITIALISED one, and which should win differs per field.
_watch: 1836.2.1 and NOT day 0: construction goods spend is exactly £0 on 1836.1.1 because the sector has not ticked (FINDINGS F14), so day 0 is history-faithful and economically unfinished. Whether the savegame diverges much from the history-derived state is itself the question — urban-centre levels and the pop-class split are the two most likely to move.
_cost: 3 runs x 2 in-game months, ~3 minutes. extract_measured averages field by field, which is its documented default because the 1836 start is nearly deterministic for most metrics but NOT all (urban-centre tram levels swing by a third between runs, F16).
_caveats: GAME 1.13.10. Metric set matches the belgium_check/allmarkets_popsol lineage that produced the current measured_1836.json, so the two are comparable field by field. Tags are the eight preset countries, which is what config/presets.json drives. ⚠ n=3 because the FIRST single-run attempt showed military type counts and trade breadth well below the committed reference, which is exactly the shape single-run coverage noise takes; averaging is how extract_measured is meant to be fed. ⚠⚠ WAGES IS A BURST METRIC: telemetry_lib restricts its PER-POP sweep to ENDPOINT dumps because a dump writes its lines in ONE tick and the log ring is shared and finite (landmine L4/L9). This run puts the per-pop sweep in the same tick as SCEN/BINV/POP/THRU, which is exactly the eviction risk. VERIFY AFTERWARDS: SCEN lines must still read ~570 per run, as they did at n=3. If they drop, the wage sweep evicted the scenario metrics and wages must be run separately and merged with -WagesOnly.
